title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 167
paragraphs: At the time of which I am speaking, however, this Aryandes had pity on Pheretime and gave her all the forces in Egypt, both land and sea, appointing Amasis, a Maraphian, to command the land-army and Badres, of the Pasargadae clan, to command the fleet. But before he sent off the army, Aryandes dispatched a herald to Barca and asked who it was that had killed Arcesilaus. The men of Barca all took it upon themselves, saying that they had previously suffered many great wrongs at his hands. Hearing this, Aryandes at last sent off the army with Pheretime. This charge, then, was the pretext; but in fact the army was being sent out, as I believe, to subdue Libya. For the Libyans are divided into many nations of many kinds, and few of them were subjects of the king, while the greater number paid no heed to Darius.
